svg.text: A field guide to the Somatic Loom's engram: what lies on the ground, what floats above it, and how a weave goes.
Gaze at it with the staff
Looks like a real one, but its

to it replays the wrong memory.
Dead clot. No lane can pass
from the rim with pale spore
Pick the memory, then feed the loom its
enzymes. Each enzyme is 3 spans of thread of
its tendency. The loom tells you exactly how
many spans YOUR engram needs before taking
The engram unfurls over the ground around the
loom: an eight-pointed star of empty channels
in living skin. One fragment rises at a point
for every enzyme the recipe lists.
Staff in hand, rest your gaze on a fragment
for half a second. The echo above the loom
replays its memory. A false fragment replays
the wrong one and pulses off-beat.
Use the staff on a fragment to pick up its
lane (its pool grows a ring of beads).
Hold use and sweep along the lines node to
node, or click node by node. Sweep back onto
the last node to undo a step; sneak-use on a
lane cuts it back to that node.
A lane is home when it runs down a spoke into
the loom, or joins a lane of its own colour
that is home. Each node a lane crosses costs 1
Don't thread false fragments home. Doing so
tears them loose and costs you, by rank (see
When every real fragment is home, the engram
draws back into the loom, the spans of the
real lanes are spent, and the memory is woven.
Lanes run only along the drawn lines: the star's lines, the outer rim between neighbouring points, and the eight spokes into the loom.
A node holds one colour. Lanes of different colours never cross or share a node.
Same colour may join: end your lane on a lane of its own colour and that lane carries yours home.
Keyed engrams (Summa and up): each spoke enters one face of the loom, and a lane must enter the face of its own colour. Inner socket rims and the
loom's rim show each face's colour; the pale double ring marks the Animus face, and the wheel runs clockwise from it.
You need thread: a step is refused if the loom holds no more spans of that colour. Enzymes can be topped up mid-weave.

A weave never kills: at worst you black out.
